````js
  /* ── one clock, and it has a break in it ────────────────────────────────────
     🔴 THE MAZE HAS NO LENGTH IN THE SCORE, AND A PICTURE THAT GIVES IT A WIDTH
     INVENTS THE ONE NUMBER THE SCORE REFUSES TO STATE. `durationHow` is
     `absent`, `durationMs` is `null`, and the only line in the file with a
     negative time asks the visitor to walk towards the stairs. So the maze runs
     until a person moves, and nothing anybody can write down says how long that
     is.

     That is why every scene, event and spoken line in the data carries
     `at: { fromIntroMs, fromMazeEndMs }` with exactly one of the two filled in.
     The intro and the maze are placed from the intro's first keystroke;
     everything after the maze is placed from the END of the maze. Two origins,
     because one clock cannot hold both.

     WHAT THIS PAGE DRAWS is the axis the data itself states: the running order
     with the maze taken out, 12:55.2 from the first keystroke to the end of the
     outro. The maze is a BREAK in that axis, drawn as a hatched column whose
     width is in PIXELS and never in milliseconds, so it claims no duration at
     any zoom. Left of the break the clock reads from the intro; right of it,
     from the end of the maze.

     ⚠️ AND THE BREAK IS NOT EMPTY. Two things happen inside the maze and
     neither can be placed on this clock: the outer maze begins 60 s in, and the
     one line that waits for a visitor is spoken there. They are named under the
     picture rather than drawn at a position that would be a guess. */
````

## held-8: demo/held/index.html, inline script, line 161

````js
  /* ── ink ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     🔴 THE WHOLE PICTURE IS ONE INK EXCEPT FOR THE TINT LANE, AND THAT LANE IS
     A DELIBERATE EXCEPTION TO THIS PROJECT'S COLOUR RULE. The standing rule is
     that a mark's colour says HOW IT LANDED and never which lane it is in,
     because lane identity is already carried by the row, the name in the gutter
     and the swatch beside it.

     Here nothing landed. A score is a document: no scene was measured, no line
     was timed against anything, and there is no quality for a hue to report. So
     every lane is drawn in one restrained ink and strength is used where two
     kinds of mark have to be told apart.

     The exception is the tint lane, where the colour IS the fact being
     reported: the score sets a named colour lookup table on the passthrough
     image per scene, and neutral, green, blue and red are what it calls them.
     Drawing that lane in grey and writing the colour underneath would be a
     legend for a fact the picture could simply carry. Because it is the only
     coloured lane on the page, a hue anywhere else cannot be mistaken for
     identity, which is what the rule exists to prevent.

     ⚠️ THE BREAK IS THE SITE'S OWN ACCENT AND THAT IS NOT A THIRD MEANING. It
     is furniture rather than a mark: it says the axis has been cut here, it is
     the one thing on the page a reader has to notice, and `--hi` is what this
     site uses for the one thing that matters on a page. Nothing is positioned
     by it and nothing is measured in it. */
````

## held-10: demo/held/index.html, inline script, line 210

````js
  /* ── the picture over the line, and the one arithmetic in it ───────────────
     🔴 A COLOUR LOOKUP TABLE IS THREE INDEPENDENT GAINS, and the picture
     applies it as exactly that: the room's red, green and blue are multiplied
     separately, and the result is dimmed by the other channel.

         out = clamp(room * gain) * opacity

     A flat canvas does that as easily as it dims, which is what makes a picture
     of this piece possible at all on a screen.

     ⚠️ A WEB PAGE IN A HEADSET COULD NOT, AND THAT IS A LIMIT OF THE WEB AND
     NEVER OF THE WORK. A passthrough session composites a page over the room as
     `c * a + room * (1 - a)`, so the real room only ever reaches the eye
     multiplied by one scalar shared by all three colours: such a page can dim
     the room and lay a colour over it, and cannot give its three channels three
     different gains. Held in Human is a Unity application and really does put a
     colour table on the camera image. The wording matters in both directions:
     it is `a web page in a headset`, never `a headset`.

     ⚠️ THE PAGE USED TO DRAW BOTH ARITHMETICS SIDE BY SIDE and it was cut on
     2026-09-20, on the reader's verdict rather than on a measurement: *"I sid
     not get two panels reasoning. Keep ot simple."* The comparison had to be
     taught before it could be looked at. Part 2 §1 of
     `plans/plan-held-in-human-score.md` (the 2D reading, merged there 2026-10-14)
     keeps the whole argument, one log line at the foot of this file says the
     short of it, and the picture draws what the score says.

     🔴 THE FOUR TABLES ARE OUR READING OF FOUR WORDS. The score names
     `neutral`, `green`, `blue` and `red` and carries no table, no curve, no
     coefficient and no image, so every number below is this page's invention
     and none of it is the piece's. There is a check at the foot that reads that
     absence off the file rather than leaving it as a sentence.
     ⚠️ `neutral` IS THE IDENTITY, AND THAT IS A READING TOO. In colour work a
     neutral table is usually the one that changes nothing, so a neutral scene
     here is the room's own tones with only the dimming on them.
     ⚠️ NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH `TINT` ABOVE, which is the four swatches the
     tint LANE is drawn in. These are gains on a room; those are ink on a
     chart. */
````

````js
     them. There is one arithmetic now and nothing to separate. */
````
